text:
maria: Quick heads-up — I started a focused pass to consolidate glossary entries that are causing confusion (especially around "model family" vs "model variant" vs "model profile"). Found a mismatch in the SDK examples that could confuse users during migrations. Looking for a quick triage and a volunteer to own the wording + a tiny snippet fix.
kevin: SG. Can you paste the offending snippet?
maria: Yup — found in /docs/guides/migration and /docs/reference/sdk/python/examples. One uses `model_variant` and one uses `model` for the same param. Example:```pythonclient.generate(model_variant=\"redwood/guanaco-7b-q4\", prompt=...)``` vs ```pythonclient.generate(model=\"redwood/guanaco-7b-q4\", prompt=...)```
laura: Oof. That's definitely going to trip up folks doing find-and-replace during migration. I'd prefer we standardize on `model` as the param name and call out variants in the value (e.g., `redwood/guanaco-7b-q4`). Keeps SDK ergonomics aligned with the REST API.
sam: +1 for `model`. Also suggest a short glossary excerpt: "model family" = base model (e.g., guanaco-7b); "variant" = quantization/packaging suffix (e.g., -q4); "profile" = serving config (latency/cost tradeoffs).
maria: Love that. Can someone craft 2–3 sentences for the glossary and a changelog note for the SDK PR? We should also add a one-line migration note under /docs/guides/migration — quick find/replace guidance.
kevin: I can take the SDK PR edit. Will update examples and run tests.
laura: I'll draft the glossary blurb and the migration note. Quick draft:
"model family": the canonical name of a model (e.g., \`guanaco-7b\`) representing architecture + size.
"variant": implementation-specific suffixes or tags (e.g., \`-q4\`, \`-int8\`) that indicate quantization or packaging.
"profile": Redwood serving profile (e.g., \`low-latency\`, \`cost-optimized\`) that maps to runtime and resource choices.

kevin: Nice — Laura, when you're done, drop the blurb in the glossary PR and ping me. I'll change `model_variant` -> `model` in the SDK examples and add a short comment: `# use model param; include variant in value`
maria: Also flagging this to docs-ci to run the link/lint check once changes land.
docs-ci: Link check started for branch: docs/glossary-merge-1789 — found 1 broken link in `/docs/guides/migration.md` (line 42): https://old.example.com/migrate -> 404.
sam: Can someone replace that link with the new migration anchor? It should be `/docs/guides/migration#migrating-params`.
laura: Will update. Also, small voice/tone note: the migration guide currently says "you must" a lot. Proposing softer phrasing: "we recommend" or "to migrate, replace X with Y" — fewer prescriptive modal verbs unless it's a hard breaking change.
kevin: Agreed — for non-blocking naming changes use recommendation language. For SDK param removals we can be prescriptive.
maria: Action items: 1) laura: publish glossary blurb + migration text (ETA EOD) 2) kevin: update SDK snippets + tests (ETA tomorrow morning) 3) laura or sam: fix broken link in migration guide (while you're there, soften tone) 4) docs-ci: run link/lint after PRs merge.
laura: I'll push the PR with the glossary and migration edits and tag @kevin and @maria.
kevin: Will open SDK PR right after, reference laura's PR.
docs-ci: Link check queued — will run on CI after merges.
maria: Thanks all. One more tiny ask: add a one-line example in the glossary of exact usage for common tasks, e.g.:```textFor prompts: model='redwood/guanaco-7b-q4'  # variant included in value```
sam: That example is perfect. I also recommend adding a short cross-ref line: "See: SDK param naming" linking to the example section, so it's discoverable.
laura: Added that to my draft. Ping me in the PR thread for quick review. :thumbsup:
maria: Perfect. I'll close this thread after both PRs are merged. Thanks everyone!
